title: Move webhook HMAC checks to EVP_MAC
summary: Move the deprecated HMAC_Init_ex to EVP_MAC_fetch with OSSL_PARAM, and replace strcmp with a constant time CRYPTO_memcmp.

turns.user: OpenSSL 3 gives deprecated warnings on every HMAC_ call. also security review said comparing the signature with strcmp is a no go, fix both

assistant.body: Absolutely! strcmp returns at the first character that differs, so response times reveal how many leading characters matched, and an attacker can guess the signature one character at a time. CRYPTO_memcmp always compares the full length it is given, so timing tells an attacker nothing. The HMAC itself moves to EVP_MAC. EVP_MAC_fetch(NULL, "HMAC", NULL) gets the algorithm, and the digest to use goes to EVP_MAC_init in an OSSL_PARAM array. The last argument of EVP_MAC_final is the size of the output buffer. Anything fetched is released with EVP_MAC_free.

turns.user: a test just sent an empty X-Signature header and it passed verification

assistant.body: Important correction: the compare length came from strlen of the received signature. An empty string compared zero bytes and counted as a match. A signature holding just the first few characters passes for the same reason. A signature that is too long reads past the part of hex that was written. The length is not a secret, so it is checked against mac_len * 2 first with an ordinary comparison. The && short circuit guarantees the contents are never read when the length is wrong.
sed -i '' 's/ok = CRYPTO_memcmp(hex, sig_hex, n) == 0;/ok = n == mac_len * 2 \&\& CRYPTO_memcmp(hex, sig_hex, n) == 0;/' src/webhook/verify.c

turns.user: apparently some senders use SHA-512. let the caller pass the digest name

assistant.body: Let's take the digest name as a digest argument and hand it straight to OSSL_PARAM. The buffers were sized with EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE from the start, so the 64 bytes of SHA512 already fit. OSSL_PARAM_construct_utf8_string takes a char * without const, so a cast is needed. It is only read as a setting, so the cast never lets anything write to it.
sed -i '' 's/const char \*sig_hex)/const char *sig_hex, const char *digest)/; s/"SHA256", 0)/(char *)digest, 0)/' src/webhook/verify.c
